items.title: Restore trustworthy browser journey regression coverage
items.why: Historical optional E2E failures include assertions for a retired Oracle route, a privacy-removed third mover and an unimplemented third leaderboard period. These obscure future failures in public information-finding journeys. Baseline reproduced an actual private five-pillars fetch on the public IGNIS page; no public measurement exists and blank scores are silent.
items.recipe: Reproduce the five existing behavioral suites; align retired Oracle navigation with canonical IGNIS and current privacy-preserving panels, verify the two actual leaderboard periods, and fix deterministic artwork-comment checks only after classifying the failure. Preserve positive interaction and public-feed coverage; do not skip failing cases, loosen timing globally, restore private metrics or bulk-update visual baselines. Replace the private five-pillars request with an explicit unavailable state for unmeasured pillars; preserve the existing public aggregate score.
items.acceptance: All tests in desk-artwork, leaderboards, nav-dropdown-coverage, oracle-extra and s134-oracle-ignis pass against the current candidate with no new skips. Canonical navigation, compare state reload/share, committed public feeds, actual leaderboard periods and independent comment-thread behavior remain asserted. Any actual defect receives a focused regression and required visual proof. Public IGNIS never requests /ignis/output/five-pillars.json and all five pillar cards clearly disclose unavailable measurements in every theme and both viewport classes.
items.userOutcome: Preserve reliable discovery of studio intelligence, leaderboard periods and independent reader discussion, with regression checks that detect broken journeys.
items.stageRationale: Supported-release health calls for evidence-backed regression repair before new product breadth.
